title: AMD Stock Falls 1.8% as Chip Stocks Slide (Nov 25)
summary: AMD stock closed at $406.03 on Nov 25, down 1.75%, after recovering most of an early drop as chip stocks sold off on AI spending, tariff and rate worries.
body_markdown:
As reported by[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-november-25-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-pce-inflation-data-091428237.html) , the Trump administration unveiled new 20% tariffs on China, the European Union and 12 other major US trading partners, to be stacked on existing rates and to take effect after a public comment period, in January at the earliest. The same day's PCE data showed price increases picked up in October, which Yahoo Finance said raised expectations that the Fed will have to raise rates next month, while chip stocks trimmed earlier losses by the close. The US 10-year Treasury yield ended the session at 4.85%, down 6.0 basis points.


The session also followed earlier pressure on the stock. Per[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/25/amd-stock-would-need-to-rise-about-57-to-get-back-to-its-record-history-says-how-long-past-comebacks-took/?source=iedfolrf0000001) , AMD fell after a November 19 short-seller report from Hunterbrook, and a[broad sell-off in chip stocks on Tuesday](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-nvda-stock-news-november-25-2026/) pushed it back near its November 5 close.


## AMD Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- AMD's third-quarter 2026 revenue climbed 45% year over year to a record $13.4 billion, per The Motley Fool.
- Management expects roughly $17 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, which The Motley Fool said implies growth of about 66% year over year.
- The data center segment, which includes AI chips and server processors, almost doubled from the year-ago quarter to $8.5 billion, The Motley Fool reported.


### Risks


- Doubts over the returns on AI spending, new tariff plans and rate-hike expectations weighed on chip stocks through the session, per Investing.com and Yahoo Finance.
- Hunterbrook, which disclosed a short position, alleged that a blacklisted Chinese server maker kept getting newer AMD firmware. AMD said the claims misrepresent its business and that it follows US export laws, and none of the allegations has been proven, The Motley Fool reported.
- In a[registration statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000002488/000119312526472370/d171551ds3asr.htm) filed on November 23, AMD registered up to 336,934,324 shares for resale by selling stockholders, including up to 160 million shares each that OpenAI and[Meta Platforms (META)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/meta/) may acquire if their warrants vest and are exercised, plus shares issued in the Taalas and World Labs acquisitions. AMD receives no proceeds from any sale by these holders.
